mission_title: Package H Batch 03 Runtime Owner Closure Mission Definition
strategic_context: Package H Batch 02 established owner-neutral onboarding declarations and evidence. Batch 03 exists to define the governed mission for runtime owner closure without beginning architecture, blueprint, or implementation.
business_justification: SHS BOS needs a governed path for future owner activation readiness so integrations remain replaceable, evidence-backed, and neutral.
engineering_justification: Future runtime owner closure must preserve the certified extension-kernel boundary, existing registries, and canonical runtime owners before any design or code begins.
problem_statement: Runtime owner closure can drift into marketplace ownership, duplicate registries, premature activation, APIs, UI, or persistence unless Phase 1 locks purpose and boundaries first.
opportunity_statement: A complete Phase 1 mission lets independent teams produce substantially equivalent architecture charters under IGLS-1.
desired_future_state: Batch 03 may proceed only to an Architecture Charter that maps runtime owner closure against existing authorities while preserving neutral infrastructure.
mission_scope: define what Batch 03 may evaluate in Phase 2
define boundaries, risks, evidence, and authorization logic
assumptions: Batch 02 and IGLS-1 governing commits remain immutable references
future Phase 2 work will be separately authorized
Batch 03 will not infer implementation approval from mission approval
constraints: no architecture may begin in Phase 1
no duplicate constitutional authority may be introduced
known_risks: runtime owner closure could be misread as activation approval
Package H could drift into marketplace ownership
architecture could duplicate existing runtime owners
known_unknowns: future interaction with downstream Package G
success_criteria: evidence strategy fixed for future phases
only IGLS-1 Phase 2 Architecture Charter authorized
mission_completion_definition: Phase 1 is complete when mission, alignment, boundary, risk, evidence, authorization, traceability, and independent certification artifacts pass validation.
acceptance_strategy: Validate completeness, constitutional alignment, boundary integrity, evidence completeness, authorization logic, and absence of implementation.
evidence_strategy: Use repository-grounded artifacts, exact baselines, validator output, and independent certification.
certification_strategy: Separate reviewer certifies artifacts and validator results without modifying repository state.
publication_strategy: No publication or tag is authorized by Phase 1 unless separately requested by release governance.
